settings.name: AI_MaxAttempts
settings.label: AI call attempts
settings.description: Attempts for each AI call (default 4).
settings.purpose: How many times Risk Analysis tries an AI request when the AI service times out, throttles or has a temporary failure.
settings.effect: More attempts make the AI summary more likely to succeed under load, but a failing service makes the run take longer. Other errors fail at once regardless.
settings.whenToChange: Raise if AI summaries often fail on throttling or timeouts.

info.what: How many times Risk Analysis tries an AI request when the AI service times out, throttles or has a temporary failure.
info.whenChanged: More attempts make the AI summary more likely to succeed under load, but a failing service makes the run take longer. Other errors fail at once regardless.
info.risk: Affects whether and how AI is used: when AI is used, asset data is sent to YOUR Azure OpenAI deployment, and it costs per call. Reversible at once; results already produced stay.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Raise if AI summaries often fail on throttling or timeouts.

settings.name: AutoBucketCache
settings.label: Remember query split counts
settings.defaultText: On: split counts are saved and reused.
settings.description: reuse last-known-good bucket count
settings.purpose: Saves how many parts each large risk analysis query had to be split into, so later runs start at the right number.
settings.effect: Off, every run probes again from one part upward, which makes large estates noticeably slower. On, a changed query is detected and re-probed automatically.
settings.whenToChange: Rarely; turn off only while troubleshooting query splitting.

info.what: Saves how many parts each large risk analysis query had to be split into, so later runs start at the right number.
info.whenOn: split counts are saved and reused.

info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Rarely; turn off only while troubleshooting query splitting.

settings.name: AutoBucketChallenger_ConfirmDays
settings.label: Split count re-test pause
settings.description: ... and at most once in this many days after a run decided the count.
settings.purpose: After a run decided a report's split count, how many days pass before a suspiciously high count is tested again.
settings.effect: Shorter re-tests a count that looks too high sooner, at the cost of extra queries; longer keeps a wrong count longer.
settings.whenToChange: Rarely; only with support while tuning query splitting.

info.what: After a run decided a report's split count, how many days pass before a suspiciously high count is tested again.
info.whenChanged: Shorter re-tests a count that looks too high sooner, at the cost of extra queries; longer keeps a wrong count longer.

settings.name: AutoBucketChallenger_MedianMultiplier
settings.label: Split count re-test threshold
settings.description: Re-test of a suspicious split count: a count this many times the median of the other reports is re-tested ...

settings.effect: Lower re-tests more reports (more queries); higher re-tests only extreme counts.

settings.name: Mail_CloseLoop_Daily_SendMail
settings.label: Send the daily vulnerability mail
settings.description: SERVICENOW -- ONE ROUTE (#914). SecurityInsight never writes ServiceNow configuration items or vulnerable items itself: it delivers to STAGING -- the hand-off database (SQL views ServiceNow imports through a JDBC data source) or the ServiceNow data-out connector (Import Set tables, the SI_DataOut_ServiceNow* settings above) -- and ServiceNow's own import / transform rules make every change. The older push and its settings (SI_ServiceNow_ImportSetTable, SI_ServiceNow_ImportSetMaxRows, SI_VulnSync_ServiceNowImportSetTable, SI_ServiceNow_DirectWrite, SI_VulnSync_ServiceNowDirectWrite) were removed. The vulnerability close-loop's DAILY MAIL (Pro; edited on the management GUI's e-mail settings page): the last 24 hours' opened, closed and reopened vulnerabilities by severity and asset tier, what is open now, and the mean time to fix, sent after the close-loop run through the same relay as the Risk Analysis mail. Off by default.
settings.purpose: Sends one mail a day with the vulnerabilities opened, closed and reopened in the last 24 hours, what is open now and the mean time to fix.
settings.effect: On: a daily job mails the summary to the close-loop recipients through the same mail server as the Risk Analysis mail. Nothing is sent without recipients.
settings.whenToChange: Turn on when the team should get a daily view of vulnerability progress.

info.what: Sends one mail a day with the vulnerabilities opened, closed and reopened in the last 24 hours, what is open now and the mean time to fix.

info.whenOff: Off is the default: none of what "On" describes happens.
info.risk: A wrong value can mean that alerts and reports go to the wrong people or to nobody, or that mail stops; no collected data is changed. Reversible at once: change it back.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Turn on when the team should get a daily view of vulnerability progress.

settings.name: SI_AISummary_Leader
settings.label: Leading report for AI summary
settings.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view
settings.description: WHICH REPORT IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH in 'Consistent' mode. The leader always builds its own figures and never adopts anyone else's; the other report adopts the leader's. Default 'Summary', because that is the grain an executive audience usually reads -- set 'Detailed' if your management receives the Detailed report instead and the relationship inverts cleanly. There is deliberately NO time window deciding who wins. An earlier design said "the first report of the cycle wins", but a cycle cannot be identified from a clock: your two runs may legitimately fall on different UTC days (Summary late evening, Detailed early morning), and a long run can straddle midnight by itself. Naming a leader removes the question entirely -- the pairing survives any schedule, timezone or run duration, and the follower's figures can never appear in the leader's mail.
settings.purpose: In Consistent mode, chooses which report (Summary or Detailed) builds the AI summary, risk score and top list that the other report reuses.
settings.effect: The leading report always computes its own figures; the other copies them so both mails agree. An unknown value falls back to Detailed with a warning. Ignored in PerReport mode. With the Summary step off (the default) only the Detailed report runs, so it always leads.
settings.whenToChange: Set to Summary only when the Summary step is switched on and management mainly receives the Summary report.

info.what: In Consistent mode, chooses which report (Summary or Detailed) builds the AI summary, risk score and top list that the other report reuses.
info.whenChanged: The leading report always computes its own figures; the other copies them so both mails agree. An unknown value falls back to Detailed with a warning. Ignored in PerReport mode. With the Summary step off (the default) only the Detailed report runs, so it always leads.
info.risk: Changes how the headline figures are presented in the mails and the executive view; the findings themselves are unchanged. Reversible at once.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Set to Summary only when the Summary step is switched on and management mainly receives the Summary report.

settings.name: SI_AISummary_Mode
settings.label: Summary and Detailed agreement
settings.group: Risk Analysis -- mails and executive view
settings.defaultText: Depends on the edition. SecurityInsight Pro: PerReport -- each report shows its own figures (Summary counts distinct assets, Detailed counts individual findings). Community: Consistent -- both reports show the same figures. A value you set wins in both editions.
settings.description: --- AI executive summary (RA) --------------------------------------------- HOW THE SUMMARY AND DETAILED REPORTS RELATE TO EACH OTHER. The two reports count different things and always will: Summary counts distinct ASSETS, Detailed counts individual ASSET FINDINGS (one asset can carry many). The same estate therefore produces different totals and percentages in the two reports. What you choose here is whether the two reports are made to AGREE, or whether each simply reports its own grain. Either way both mails now carry a line under the KPI explaining why the figures differ. 'Consistent' (Community default) -- the leading report builds the AI narrative, the headline Risk Score KPI and the Top-50 list, and the other report REUSES them verbatim, so both mails show identical figures. Choose this where management receives BOTH reports. 'PerReport' (Pro default) -- each report computes and shows its own numbers and never adopts the other's. Choose this where management receives ONE report, or where each report should be true to its own grain. Leave unset for the edition's default: 'Consistent' in Community -- what every install did before this setting existed, so upgrading changes nothing -- and 'PerReport' in SecurityInsight Pro, where the web app shows Summary and Detailed side by side. A value you set here wins in both editions.
settings.purpose: Chooses whether the Summary and Detailed reports show identical AI summary, risk score and top list, or each shows its own figures.
settings.effect: Consistent makes one report reuse the other's figures, saving AI calls. PerReport makes each report compute its own, so totals differ. Unknown values fall back to the edition's default.
settings.whenToChange: Choose PerReport when each audience receives only one report, or (Pro) to compare Summary and Detailed in the web app. Choose Consistent when management receives both mails and they must show the same figures.

settings.name: SI_AssetProperties
settings.label: Asset properties
settings.defaultText: security: the security profile only -- what SecurityInsight needs for risk
settings.description: Asset properties, two levels. 'security' (the default) = what SecurityInsight needs for risk: the profilers read their sources exactly as always and nothing extra is stored. 'full' = each profiler reads each source ONCE with every property, builds the same security profile from it, and publishes the whole object (Defender, Entra, Intune, AD, Azure, Exposure Graph, VM extensions) to SI_AssetProperties_CL for the CMDB hand-off; (Pro) the data sync stores every snapshot for the web app's asset page, with its history.
settings.purpose: How much SecurityInsight keeps about each asset: security (what SecurityInsight needs for risk) or full (all metadata from every source, kept a few days).
settings.effect: 'security' (the default) keeps what SecurityInsight needs for risk -- name, kind, tier and the security fields each profile carries -- and stores nothing extra. 'full' also keeps every property each source knows about an asset -- Defender, Entra, Intune, Active Directory, Azure, Exposure Graph and VM extensions, including serial numbers and MAC addresses. Each source is still read only once: the profiler reads it with every property and builds the same security profile from it, so the profile does not change. The whole objects go to SI_AssetProperties_CL for the CMDB and vulnerability hand-off, and the data sync stores them in the Pro database, where the asset page shows them under "Full metadata" per source (lists stay lists), with a history of every snapshot kept and what changed between them. It is kept for the days set in "Full asset metadata: days kept" (default 3). Full adds Log Analytics ingest on every run; switching back to security stops the collection, and what was stored ages out after those days.
settings.whenToChange: Choose full when you want to see every property of an asset in the web app, or when SecurityInsight should hand asset metadata to a CMDB (for example ServiceNow); leave security otherwise.

settings.name: SI_AssetProperties_RetentionDays
settings.label: Full asset metadata: days kept
settings.description: Days the full asset metadata is kept -- in Log Analytics (the table's retention, set by the run; Log Analytics keeps a table at least 4 days, so a lower value is raised to 4) and in the Pro database (pruned by the data sync). Default 3.
settings.purpose: How many days the full asset metadata is kept, in Log Analytics and in the Pro database.
settings.effect: The run sets the retention of SI_AssetProperties_CL to this many days (Log Analytics keeps a table at least 4 days, so a lower value is raised to 4 and the run says so), and the data sync removes older full metadata from the Pro database. Every snapshot inside these days is kept, so the asset page's history goes back this far. The data is only needed for the hand-off, the history and the change guard, so a short retention keeps the cost low.
settings.whenToChange: Raise it only if the full asset metadata must be looked up further back.

info.what: How many days the full asset metadata is kept, in Log Analytics and in the Pro database.
info.whenChanged: The run sets the retention of SI_AssetProperties_CL to this many days (Log Analytics keeps a table at least 4 days, so a lower value is raised to 4 and the run says so), and the data sync removes older full metadata from the Pro database. info.risk: Changes how long data is kept or how quickly assets are treated as gone. Shortening a retention DELETES older data at the next clean-up and that cannot be undone; shortening a grace period retires assets (and closes their findings) sooner. Lengthening is safe but uses more storage.

settings.name: SI_BucketLateRetries
settings.label: Risk Analysis late bucket retries
settings.description: --- risk analysis ----------------------------------------------------------- Late retries of a bucket that failed transiently, after the main pass (default 3).
settings.purpose: How many extra attempts a query slice gets at the end of a Risk Analysis report when it failed earlier because the service was throttling or unavailable.
settings.effect: More attempts recover more slices on a busy tenant but lengthen the run (each waits up to 10 minutes). Fewer, or 0, ends sooner but the rows of a failed slice are missing from the report.
settings.whenToChange: Most installs never should. Raise it if reports often miss rows because of throttling.

info.what: How many extra attempts a query slice gets at the end of a Risk Analysis report when it failed earlier because the service was throttling or unavailable.
info.whenChanged: More attempts recover more slices on a busy tenant but lengthen the run (each waits up to 10 minutes). Fewer, or 0, ends sooner but the rows of a failed slice are missing from the report.
info.risk: Changes what the Risk Analysis reports show, how findings are filtered or scored, or where reports go, from the next run; earlier reports are unchanged. Hiding findings can make real exposure invisible to readers. Reversible: change it back.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Most installs never should. Raise it if reports often miss rows because of throttling.

settings.name: SI_BucketOverflowRetries

settings.purpose: How many times a Risk Analysis query slice that the service answers as too large is sent at the same size before it is split into smaller slices. 1 splits it on the first too-large answer.
settings.effect: Higher sends the same too-large request again, after a 30 s and then a 60 s pause, before splitting it. The same request at the same size fails the same way, so this only adds time. Throttling, timeouts and service errors are retried separately (Risk Analysis transient error retries).
settings.whenToChange: Most installs never should. Keep 1.

info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Most installs never should. Keep 1.

settings.whenToChange: Most installs never should. Raise it on tenants with frequent temporary service errors.

settings.name: SI_CiBuild_FullReconcileDays
settings.label: CI build: days between full rebuilds
settings.defaultText: 7 days: every CI is rebuilt at least once a week; the days between build only what changed
settings.description: The CI build (correlation) rebuilds only the CIs whose records, link states, time thresholds, identity anchors or manual overrides changed since their last build; every CI is rebuilt (a full reconcile) when the last full build is this many days old, when the data model, rules, mappings or CMDB change, and after a build that failed. 0 = a full build every run.
settings.purpose: The CI build (correlation) rebuilds only the CIs whose input changed since their last build: a record new, changed, moved or gone, a link state, a time threshold, an identity anchor or a manual override. Every CI is rebuilt (a full reconcile) when the last full build is this many days old; also at once when the data model, rules, mappings or CMDB change, and after a build that failed.
settings.effect: A lower value rebuilds every CI more often (a longer correlation run on those days); 0 rebuilds every CI on every run, as before. A full reconcile that finds a CI the daily builds should have changed says so in the run log.
settings.whenToChange: Set 0 while support investigates a CI that looks out of date; otherwise keep the default.

info.what: The CI build (correlation) rebuilds only the CIs whose input changed since their last build: a record new, changed, moved or gone, a link state, a time threshold, an identity anchor or a manual override. Every CI is rebuilt (a full reconcile) when the last full build is this many days old; also at once when the data model, rules, mappings or CMDB change, and after a build that failed.
info.whenChanged: A lower value rebuilds every CI more often (a longer correlation run on those days); 0 rebuilds every CI on every run, as before. A full reconcile that finds a CI the daily builds should have changed says so in the run log.
info.risk: None to the data: a change to what the CIs are built from always rebuilds every CI on the next run; the setting only decides how often an unchanged estate is rebuilt in full. Reversible at once.
info.default: 7 days: every CI is rebuilt at least once a week; the days between build only what changed
info.recommended: Keep the default (7).

settings.name: SI_CiRulesBudgetSeconds
settings.label: CI build: time limit for the rules of one asset
settings.description: The seconds the rules of ONE asset may take in the CI build. An asset that takes longer is not fully evaluated in that run: it keeps what it had from its last complete evaluation (a new asset is left out), is named in the run log and is evaluated again in the next run -- one asset never holds the build. 0 = no limit.
settings.purpose: How long the rules of one asset may take in the CI build (correlation) before the build goes on with the next asset. Applying the rules to one asset normally takes milliseconds; an asset with unusually large data could otherwise hold the whole build, and with it every step after it.
settings.effect: An asset that takes longer is not fully evaluated in that run. Nothing of the half evaluation is stored: Risk Analysis and the views keep what the asset had from its last complete evaluation, and a new asset is left out until it is fully evaluated. It is named in the run log, counted ("N asset(s) not fully evaluated in this run") and evaluated again in the next run. A higher value gives a slow asset more time; 0 removes the limit, and one asset can then hold the build for as long as its rules take.
settings.whenToChange: Raise it when the run log names the same assets as not fully evaluated run after run and they must be included before the cause is fixed; otherwise keep the default.

info.what: How long the rules of one asset may take in the CI build (correlation) before the build goes on with the next asset. Applying the rules to one asset normally takes milliseconds; an asset with unusually large data could otherwise hold the whole build, and with it every step after it.
info.whenChanged: An asset that takes longer is not fully evaluated in that run. Nothing of the half evaluation is stored: Risk Analysis and the views keep what the asset had from its last complete evaluation, and a new asset is left out until it is fully evaluated. It is named in the run log, counted ("N asset(s) not fully evaluated in this run") and evaluated again in the next run. A higher value gives a slow asset more time; 0 removes the limit, and one asset can then hold the build for as long as its rules take.
info.risk: None to the data either way: an asset that is not fully evaluated keeps its last complete result, and no tier or finding is based on part of the rules. A very high value, or 0, lets one asset hold the build and with it the steps after it. Reversible at once.
info.recommended: Keep the default (60).

settings.name: SI_Cmdb_RetireAfterDays
settings.label: Days unseen before a CI may be retired
settings.description: The least number of days an asset must go unseen before its CI is retired (in the CI table and in the state handed to ServiceNow) -- a brake under every other rule (the grace period, the runs missing, an early retirement). Default 7, at least 1.
settings.purpose: The least number of days an asset must go unseen before its CI is retired -- in the CI table and in the state handed to ServiceNow. A brake under every other rule: whatever decided the retirement (the grace period, the runs missing, an early retirement on the Not seen anymore page), the CI waits until its asset has been unseen this long.
settings.effect: Higher keeps CIs of assets that are away for a while; a CI retired too early is the one mistake that does not heal by itself. No grace period can be shorter than this. Below 1 is raised to 1; non-numbers use 7.
settings.whenToChange: Raise it if CIs are retired for assets that come back after a week or more.

info.what: The least number of days an asset must go unseen before its CI is retired -- in the CI table and in the state handed to ServiceNow. A brake under every other rule: whatever decided the retirement (the grace period, the runs missing, an early retirement on the Not seen anymore page), the CI waits until its asset has been unseen this long.

settings.name: SI_DataOut_ServiceNowStagingStatusTable
settings.label: Data out: ServiceNow staging status table
settings.defaultText: u_si_staging_status. An install that sent to ServiceNow before the staging status table existed has it empty: the rows are sent without it, with a warning, until your ServiceNow team creates the table and you set its name here.
settings.description: The staging status table: one row when a push of an output starts (writing) and one when it ends (complete, failed or held), so your ServiceNow importer knows when a batch is complete. Every data row carries the batch id (u_si_batch_id). Not set = u_si_staging_status. '' = no staging status table: the rows are sent without it, with a warning.
settings.purpose: The ServiceNow import set table where SecurityInsight says when each push of a ServiceNow output starts (writing) and ends (complete, failed or held). Every data row carries the same batch id, so your importer imports a batch only once it is complete.
settings.effect: Set: each push is one batch -- a writing row first, the batch id on every data row, then a complete, failed or held row. If the table is missing or lacks a column, nothing is sent. Empty: the rows are sent without a batch, and the ServiceNow check warns.
settings.whenToChange: After your ServiceNow team has created the staging status table (Connectors > the ServiceNow data-out connector > For your ServiceNow team), if it has another name than the default -- or, on an install that has it empty, to switch it on.

info.what: The ServiceNow import set table where SecurityInsight says when each push of a ServiceNow output starts (writing) and ends (complete, failed or held). Every data row carries the same batch id, so your importer imports a batch only once it is complete.
info.whenChanged: Set: each push is one batch -- a writing row first, the batch id on every data row, then a complete, failed or held row. If the table is missing or lacks a column, nothing is sent. Empty: the rows are sent without a batch, and the ServiceNow check warns.
info.risk: Set to a table that does not exist on the instance, nothing is sent to ServiceNow until it is there (the ServiceNow check says why). Empty, your importer cannot tell a finished push from one that stopped halfway. Reversible at once.
info.requires: A ServiceNow output switched on (SI_DataOut_Outputs), the ServiceNow data-out connector and the table created in ServiceNow.
info.default: u_si_staging_status. An install that sent to ServiceNow before the staging status table existed has it empty: the rows are sent without it, with a warning, until your ServiceNow team creates the table and you set its name here.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: After your ServiceNow team has created the staging status table (Connectors > the ServiceNow data-out connector > For your ServiceNow team), if it has another name than the default -- or, on an install that has it empty, to switch it on.

settings.name: SI_ExcelMaxDataRows

settings.description: --- Delivery limits (added v2.2.441) -------------------------------------- Excel holds 1,048,576 rows INCLUDING the header. Above this the workbook keeps the TOP N by the sort column (highest risk first) and says how many were left out; the .json sibling and the LA ingest still carry every row.

Off by default: exempted findings are left out, and every surface says how many.

settings.effect: An exemption never removes a finding: it is kept, marked, in Log Analytics and the Pro database either way. On: they are counted everywhere by default.
settings.whenToChange: Turn on if management should see the risk including accepted exemptions.

settings.name: SI_Guards_Enabled
settings.label: All guards (safety checks)
settings.description: Every safety check can be turned on or off, and its mail turned off (Pro: Settings > Guards). Since the guard relief (2026-10-11) only the two brakes are ON by default: CIs retired by mistake (cmdb.sql.collapse, cmdb.handoff.mass-change) and duplicate vulnerability records (vuln.connector.target-incomplete); every other check is OFF until you switch it on (the examples below show the switch, not the default -- the glossary at the end says each default). Off = the check does not hold, refuse or stop: it says so once in the job log and the step goes on (config\guard-catalog .locked.json 'whenOff' says what that means per check). WARNING: SecurityInsight then acts on data that may be broken. All checks at once:
settings.purpose: One switch for every safety check that holds, refuses or stops a step to protect your data (the list below and the Guards page).
settings.effect: WARNING -- Off turns EVERY safety check off at once: SecurityInsight then closes vulnerability records, retires CIs, hands over batches and loads collections even when the data looks broken or incomplete, so a failed collection can close or retire everything it no longer sees. Nothing is held for release and no guard mail is sent; each check says once in its job log that it is off. The checks that only report a stop SecurityInsight cannot skip (the source failed, the licence) stop reporting it. On: every check works as set below.
settings.whenToChange: Leave it on. Turn it off only for a short time, when the checks stop work you know is right -- and prefer turning off or tuning the one check that is in the way.
settings.hint: Off = every check below is off.

info.risk: Turning this off removes EVERY safety check at once: no step is held or stopped to protect your data, whatever happens. Reversible at once: switch it back on; it applies from the next run.
info.recommended: Keep it on. Change it when: Leave it on. Turn it off only for a short time, when the checks stop work you know is right -- and prefer turning off or tuning the one check that is in the way.
info.confirm: WARNING -- Off turns EVERY safety check off at once: SecurityInsight then closes vulnerability records, retires CIs, hands over batches and loads collections even when the data looks broken or incomplete, so a failed collection can close or retire everything it no longer sees. info.what: Client id of a user-assigned managed identity to sign in with when the sign-in method is managed identity.

settings.name: SI_MaxMailAttachmentMB
settings.label: Largest mail attachment
settings.defaultText: 24 MB (fits a 25 MB mail server limit)
settings.description: Mail attachment budget in MB of MESSAGE, measured base64-ENCODED (attachments inflate ~37%, so a 20 MB file is ~27 MB on the wire). Over budget, the report is sent WITHOUT the attachment rather than the relay rejecting the whole mail.
settings.purpose: The largest Excel attachment, measured as encoded for mail, that a Risk Analysis mail carries; larger reports are mailed without the attachment.
settings.effect: Raising it lets bigger workbooks be attached, but above your mail server's limit the whole mail is rejected and nothing arrives. Lowering it is always safe.
settings.whenToChange: Raise only if your mail server accepts larger messages; lower if mails are rejected.
settings.hint: A larger report is mailed without its Excel file.

info.what: The largest Excel attachment, measured as encoded for mail, that a Risk Analysis mail carries; larger reports are mailed without the attachment.
info.whenChanged: Raising it lets bigger workbooks be attached, but above your mail server's limit the whole mail is rejected and nothing arrives. Lowering it is always safe.
info.risk: A wrong value can mean that alerts and reports go to the wrong people or to nobody, or that mail stops; no collected data is changed. Reversible at once: change it back.
info.default: 24 MB (fits a 25 MB mail server limit)
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Raise only if your mail server accepts larger messages; lower if mails are rejected.

settings.name: SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays
settings.label: Patch cycle: catch-up after
settings.description: Patch cycle: a finding whose fix was released (or, without one dated update, that was first detected) more than this many days before the collection is Catch-up, else In monthly cycle (default 30; exactly 30 is still in the cycle).
settings.purpose: When a finding counts as catch-up instead of being fixed in the monthly patch cycle: its fix was released (the month a "October 2026 Security Updates" text names -> that month's Patch Tuesday), or -- without one dated update -- the finding was first detected, more than this many days before the collection.
settings.effect: The Patch cycle column of every finding (In monthly cycle / Catch-up / No fix available / Unknown) and its filter use this number from the next Risk Analysis run; findings already stored keep the value they were given.
settings.whenToChange: Match your patch policy: e.g. 45 when monthly patches are allowed six weeks.

info.what: When a finding counts as catch-up instead of being fixed in the monthly patch cycle: its fix was released (the month a "October 2026 Security Updates" text names -> that month's Patch Tuesday), or -- without one dated update -- the finding was first detected, more than this many days before the collection.
info.whenChanged: The Patch cycle column of every finding (In monthly cycle / Catch-up / No fix available / Unknown) and its filter use this number from the next Risk Analysis run; findings already stored keep the value they were given.
info.risk: Changes what the Risk Analysis reports show, how findings are filtered or scored, or where reports go, from the next run; earlier reports are unchanged. Hiding findings can make real exposure invisible to readers. Reversible: change it back.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Match your patch policy: e.g. 45 when monthly patches are allowed six weeks.

settings.purpose: Reads the release date of each Microsoft update (by its KB number) from Microsoft's public Security Update Guide (api.msrc.microsoft.com, no sign-in), once a day, and keeps it in the install. Defender names the update and its KB but not when it was released.
settings.effect: On: a Microsoft fix's own release date decides In monthly cycle / Catch-up (an out-of-band update by its own date). Off: no call to api.msrc.microsoft.com; the month the update's name says (its Patch Tuesday) is used. A third-party fix uses the first detection either way.
settings.whenToChange: Turn off when the install must not call out to api.msrc.microsoft.com (a private network that does not allow it). A failed call is said once per run and the name rule is used.

info.what: Reads the release date of each Microsoft update (by its KB number) from Microsoft's public Security Update Guide (api.msrc.microsoft.com, no sign-in), once a day, and keeps it in the install. Defender names the update and its KB but not when it was released.

settings.name: SI_PayloadProfile
settings.label: Asset detail level
settings.defaultText: cmdb: every collected property is kept
settings.description: --- profile payload --------------------------------------------------------- 'cmdb' (default) = every collected property; 'security' = only the schema-declared columns (default-deny, smaller).
settings.purpose: Chooses how much detail is kept per asset: everything collected (cmdb) or only the columns the schema declares (security).
settings.effect: security gives smaller rows and lower ingest cost, but drops undeclared properties that queries or dashboards may use; dropped fields are listed in the run log. An unknown value falls back to cmdb.
settings.whenToChange: Consider security only if ingest volume matters more than a full asset inventory.

info.what: Chooses how much detail is kept per asset: everything collected (cmdb) or only the columns the schema declares (security).
info.whenChanged: security gives smaller rows and lower ingest cost, but drops undeclared properties that queries or dashboards may use; dropped fields are listed in the run log. An unknown value falls back to cmdb.
info.risk: Changes how long data is kept or how quickly assets are treated as gone. Shortening a retention DELETES older data at the next clean-up and that cannot be undone; shortening a grace period retires assets (and closes their findings) sooner. Lengthening is safe but uses more storage.
info.default: cmdb: every collected property is kept
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Consider security only if ingest volume matters more than a full asset inventory.

settings.name: SI_Pipeline_StartTime

A pipeline already stored (Operations > Jobs, or config\job-flow.custom.json) keeps its own time. The guided installer asks for the time zone.
settings.purpose: The time of day a new install's daily pipeline (Collect, Correlate, Deliver) starts, in the pipeline's time zone.
settings.effect: The pipeline starts at this local time every day; summer time moves the time in UTC, never the local time. A pipeline already stored on Operations > Jobs or in config\job-flow.custom.json keeps its own time -- change that one there.

info.what: The time of day a new install's daily pipeline (Collect, Correlate, Deliver) starts, in the pipeline's time zone.
info.whenChanged: The pipeline starts at this local time every day; summer time moves the time in UTC, never the local time. A pipeline already stored on Operations > Jobs or in config\job-flow.custom.json keeps its own time -- change that one there.

settings.name: SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RefreshDays
settings.label: Privilege tier catalog: days kept while unchanged
settings.defaultText: 7 days: the catalog is rebuilt as soon as a role or permission changes, and at least once a week
settings.description: Days a catalog is kept while its inputs are unchanged. Each run collects the role definitions and permission catalogs (seconds) and skips the AI pass when they, the engine and the AI settings are the same as for the last complete catalog and that catalog is younger than this. 0 = rebuild on every run.
settings.purpose: How long the privilege tier classifier keeps its catalog while nothing it is made from changed. Every run reads the Entra role definitions, the API permission catalog and the Azure role definitions (seconds); when they, the engine and the AI settings are the same as for the last complete catalog and that catalog is younger than this, the AI pass is skipped and the catalog is kept.
settings.effect: A lower value rebuilds (and sends the AI requests) more often; 0 rebuilds on every run, as before. A catalog that left items untiered is always rebuilt on the next run.
settings.whenToChange: Set 0 to rebuild every run, for example while you test new tiering prompts; raise it to cut AI calls further.

info.what: How long the privilege tier classifier keeps its catalog while nothing it is made from changed. Every run reads the Entra role definitions, the API permission catalog and the Azure role definitions (seconds); when they, the engine and the AI settings are the same as for the last complete catalog and that catalog is younger than this, the AI pass is skipped and the catalog is kept.
info.whenChanged: A lower value rebuilds (and sends the AI requests) more often; 0 rebuilds on every run, as before. A catalog that left items untiered is always rebuilt on the next run.
info.risk: None to the data: a changed role or permission always rebuilds the catalog on the next run; the setting only decides how long an unchanged catalog is kept. Reversible at once.
info.default: 7 days: the catalog is rebuilt as soon as a role or permission changes, and at least once a week
info.recommended: Keep the default (7).

settings.name: SI_PrivilegeTierClassifier_RunAI
settings.label: AI for privilege tier catalog
settings.description: Master switch. $true (default) runs all 4 AI categories; $false short-circuits to the static built-in tier map.
settings.purpose: An override for ONE engine: whether the privilege tier classifier asks Azure OpenAI to tier new roles and permissions. It follows its own switch, not AI integration: it calls AI whenever the Azure OpenAI settings are set, unless this is off.
settings.effect: Turning it off sends nothing to Azure OpenAI: roles and permissions already in the catalog keep their tier, and new ones are left unresolved for manual review. Removes AI cost for this engine.
settings.whenToChange: Only to keep AI out of the privilege tier classifier while it is used elsewhere; or turn it off if you tier new roles yourself.

info.what: An override for ONE engine: whether the privilege tier classifier asks Azure OpenAI to tier new roles and permissions. It follows its own switch, not AI integration: it calls AI whenever the Azure OpenAI settings are set, unless this is off.
info.whenOn: On is the default: it works as described under "What it does".
info.whenOff: Turning it off sends nothing to Azure OpenAI: roles and permissions already in the catalog keep their tier, and new ones are left unresolved for manual review. Removes AI cost for this engine.
info.risk: With the Azure OpenAI settings set, new role and permission names are sent to YOUR Azure OpenAI deployment, and each call costs; off leaves new ones untiered for manual review. Reversible at once.
info.recommended: Keep the default; turn it off only to keep AI out of this engine.

settings.name: SI_Pro_AssetRetire_GraceDays
settings.label: Days before an unseen asset is retired
settings.description: AN ASSET SECURITYINSIGHT NO LONGER SEES (#406): how many days an asset may go unseen before SecurityInsight retires it -- its open vulnerabilities then close as AssetRetired (never as fixed), its CI is retired, and ServiceNow gets the state (u_si_state). Seen again = active again. Default for every category; each category below can override it. Default 30.
settings.purpose: How many days an asset SecurityInsight no longer sees may stay unseen before it is retired: its open vulnerabilities close as AssetRetired (never as fixed), its CI in the CI table is retired, and ServiceNow gets the state (u_si_state = retired). Used for every category that has no value of its own.
settings.effect: Until then the asset is listed on Assets & services > CMDB > Not seen anymore with its open findings, where an Admin may retire it early. Seen again = active again, and its findings reopen. Shorter than the seen-window (8 days) is raised to the seen-window; non-numbers use 30.
settings.whenToChange: Raise it if assets are away longer than this and come back (for example laptops during a long holiday); lower it to close the findings of removed assets sooner.

info.what: How many days an asset SecurityInsight no longer sees may stay unseen before it is retired: its open vulnerabilities close as AssetRetired (never as fixed), its CI in the CI table is retired, and ServiceNow gets the state (u_si_state = retired). Used for every category that has no value of its own.
info.whenChanged: Until then the asset is listed on Assets & services > CMDB > Not seen anymore with its open findings, where an Admin may retire it early. Seen again = active again, and its findings reopen. Shorter than the seen-window (8 days) is raised to the seen-window; non-numbers use 30.
info.risk: A shorter grace period retires unseen assets sooner -- and closes their open vulnerabilities as retired. A device that is only offline for a while can be retired by mistake. Reversible for the future; closed findings reopen only when the asset is seen again.
info.recommended: 30 days (devices can be offline for weeks).
info.confirm: A shorter grace period retires unseen assets sooner -- and closes their open vulnerabilities as retired. A device that is only offline for a while can be retired by mistake. Reversible for the future; closed findings reopen only when the asset is seen again.

settings.description: Months the Pro audit trail (cfg.AuditEvent: every action in the web app, the jobs and setup) keeps its rows. Not set = kept forever. At least 13; older rows are removed only by the data sync's retention step, which records itself.
settings.purpose: How many months the Pro audit trail (every action in the web app, the jobs and setup: who, when, why, before and after) keeps its rows.
settings.effect: When set, the data sync removes audit rows older than this many months and records that removal on the trail itself. It cannot be shorter than 13 months; a smaller value or one that is not a whole number is refused and the trail is kept in full.
settings.whenToChange: Set it when your retention policy requires audit evidence to be removed after a period -- keep it at least as long as the data the trail explains.

info.what: How many months the Pro audit trail (every action in the web app, the jobs and setup: who, when, why, before and after) keeps its rows.
info.whenChanged: When set, the data sync removes audit rows older than this many months and records that removal on the trail itself. It cannot be shorter than 13 months; a smaller value or one that is not a whole number is refused and the trail is kept in full.
info.risk: Setting it, or lowering it, PERMANENTLY deletes audit rows older than this at the next sync (at least 13 months is enforced). Cannot be undone; check your audit obligations first.

info.recommended: Not set (keep the audit trail), or your audit policy's period.
info.confirm: Setting it, or lowering it, PERMANENTLY deletes audit rows older than this at the next sync (at least 13 months is enforced). Cannot be undone; check your audit obligations first.

settings.name: SI_Pro_CiChangeRetentionDays

info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Shorten it to keep the database small; lengthen it when you need a longer audit of CI changes.

settings.name: SI_Pro_CmdbSql_Kinds
settings.label: Asset kinds written as CIs
settings.description: Which kinds of asset become CIs: 'endpoint' (devices), 'azure' (Azure resources) and, if you want them, 'publicip'. Identities are never written as CIs.
settings.purpose: Which kinds of asset the SQL CMDB connector writes to the CI table: endpoint (devices), azure (Azure resources) and publicip (public IP addresses).
settings.effect: A kind you add gets its CIs on the next run. CIs of a kind you remove are kept as they are (not retired). Identities are never written as CIs; unknown values are ignored.

info.what: Which kinds of asset the SQL CMDB connector writes to the CI table: endpoint (devices), azure (Azure resources) and publicip (public IP addresses).

settings.name: SI_Pro_CmdbSql_RetireAfterRuns
settings.label: Runs before a CI is retired
settings.description: How many complete runs in a row an asset must be missing before its CI is retired (kept, never deleted). Each new snapshot counts once; a run that reads the same snapshot again counts nothing. Default 2, at least 1.
settings.purpose: How many complete runs in a row an asset must be missing before the SQL CMDB connector retires its CI.
settings.effect: Higher keeps CIs of assets that drop out now and then, but marks really removed assets as retired later. A retired CI is kept with its history and comes back if the asset is seen again. A run that reads the same snapshot as the last one does not count. Below 1 is raised to 1; non-numbers use 2.
settings.whenToChange: Raise it if CIs are retired and reactivated for assets that are still there.

info.what: How many complete runs in a row an asset must be missing before the SQL CMDB connector retires its CI.
info.whenChanged: Higher keeps CIs of assets that drop out now and then, but marks really removed assets as retired later. A retired CI is kept with its history and comes back if the asset is seen again. A run that reads the same snapshot as the last one does not count. Below 1 is raised to 1; non-numbers use 2.
info.risk: Changes how long data is kept or how quickly assets are treated as gone. Shortening a retention DELETES older data at the next clean-up and that cannot be undone; shortening a grace period retires assets (and closes their findings) sooner. Lengthening is safe but uses more storage.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Raise it if CIs are retired and reactivated for assets that are still there.

settings.name: SI_Pro_CmdbSql_SeenWithinDays
settings.label: CI seen-window
settings.description: An asset counts as present when its profile was published within this many days. Low tiers are re-profiled weekly, so keep it above the slowest tier's re-check interval. Default 8, at least 1.
settings.purpose: How recently an asset's profile must have been published for the SQL CMDB connector to count the asset as present.
settings.effect: Shorter notices removed assets sooner but can count low-tier assets as missing, because they are re-profiled only weekly. A kind whose newest snapshot is older than this is not used at all and the run changes nothing. Below 1 is raised to 1.
settings.whenToChange: Only if you changed how often low-tier assets are re-profiled; keep it above the slowest re-check interval.

info.what: How recently an asset's profile must have been published for the SQL CMDB connector to count the asset as present.
info.whenChanged: Shorter notices removed assets sooner but can count low-tier assets as missing, because they are re-profiled only weekly. A kind whose newest snapshot is older than this is not used at all and the run changes nothing. Below 1 is raised to 1.
info.risk: Changes how long data is kept or how quickly assets are treated as gone. Shortening a retention DELETES older data at the next clean-up and that cannot be undone; shortening a grace period retires assets (and closes their findings) sooner. Lengthening is safe but uses more storage.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Only if you changed how often low-tier assets are re-profiled; keep it above the slowest re-check interval.

settings.name: SI_Pro_ConfigBackupRetentionDays
settings.label: Configuration backups kept (days)
settings.description: Days the configuration backups are kept (the daily backup job and Back up now; Configuration > Backups (restore)). Default 90, at least 1. A pinned backup is kept until it is unpinned; removals are recorded on the audit trail.
settings.purpose: How many days the configuration backups are kept (the daily backup and Back up now).
settings.effect: The backup job removes backups older than this, except pinned ones and a backup whose content a newer one points at; each removal is recorded on the audit trail. A day without changes is recorded as no change, not copied again.
settings.whenToChange: When your policy needs backups for a longer or shorter time. The change journal is always kept at least this long.

info.what: How many days the configuration backups are kept (the daily backup and Back up now).
info.whenChanged: The backup job removes backups older than this, except pinned ones and a backup whose content a newer one points at; each removal is recorded on the audit trail. A day without changes is recorded as no change, not copied again.
info.risk: A shorter value deletes older configuration backups at the next backup run (pinned ones are kept). Cannot be undone.
info.recommended: 90 days.
info.confirm: A shorter value deletes older configuration backups at the next backup run (pinned ones are kept). Cannot be undone.

settings.name: SI_Pro_ConfigJournalRetentionDays
settings.label: Change journal kept (days)
settings.defaultText: not set: the change journal is kept forever
settings.description: Days the change journal (every configuration change, record by record -- what undo and restore are built on) keeps its rows. Not set = kept forever (the default). Never shorter than the backup retention: a shorter value is refused and the journal is kept.
settings.purpose: How many days the change journal keeps its rows -- every configuration change, record by record, that undo and restore are built on.
settings.effect: When set, the backup job removes journal rows older than this and records that on the audit trail. It can never be shorter than the backup retention: a shorter value is refused and the journal is kept, because an undo needs its evidence.

info.what: How many days the change journal keeps its rows -- every configuration change, record by record, that undo and restore are built on.
info.whenChanged: When set, the backup job removes journal rows older than this and records that on the audit trail. It can never be shorter than the backup retention: a shorter value is refused and the journal is kept, because an undo needs its evidence.

info.default: not set: the change journal is kept forever

settings.name: SI_Pro_DataQuality_Mail_Enabled

settings.name: SI_Pro_LifecycleStaleOpenRepair
settings.label: One-time repair of stale finding records
settings.description: REMOVE-ME once it has run everywhere: the one-time repair of finding lifecycle rows left open or mislabelled before the empty-CI-id fix. off = nothing (the default); count = read only, the data sync's log says how many rows it would change and what they would become; apply = once, after a complete collection: an empty CI id becomes none, and a finding still open under an old asset key that the newest collection reports open under its CI closes as rekeyed. Nothing is deleted.
settings.purpose: A one-time clean-up of the finding history. Before a fix of October 2026, a finding that no CI held could be closed as no longer monitored when it had only moved to a CI, and such a finding could stay open under its old asset key. This repair puts those records right once.
settings.effect: off: nothing. count: nothing is changed; the data sync's log says how many finding records the repair would change and what they would become. apply: once, after a complete collection -- a record whose CI id is empty gets none (nothing visible changes), and a finding still open under an old asset key that the newest collection reports open under its CI is closed as rekeyed (the same finding, now under its CI; not a fix). Nothing is deleted; every other record goes through the usual rule.
settings.whenToChange: Only when support asks for it: first count, then apply. It is removed in a later release once it has run everywhere.

info.what: A one-time clean-up of the finding history. Before a fix of October 2026, a finding that no CI held could be closed as no longer monitored when it had only moved to a CI, and such a finding could stay open under its old asset key. This repair puts those records right once.
info.whenChanged: off: nothing. count: nothing is changed; the data sync's log says how many finding records the repair would change and what they would become. apply: once, after a complete collection -- a record whose CI id is empty gets none (nothing visible changes), and a finding still open under an old asset key that the newest collection reports open under its CI is closed as rekeyed (the same finding, now under its CI; not a fix). Nothing is deleted; every other record goes through the usual rule.
info.risk: count changes nothing. apply changes finding records once: an empty CI id is cleared, and a finding still open under an old asset key that is open under its CI is closed as rekeyed -- its CI's own record stays open, so no finding disappears from the open list; it only stops being counted twice. Not reversible by the setting (turning it off later does not reopen them); nothing is deleted.
info.recommended: off; count first when support asks, then apply.

settings.name: SI_Pro_Pipeline_FirstRunRestarts
settings.label: First collection: restarts of a failed step
settings.description: A new install's first collection: a step that fails or is stopped is started again at once -- it carries on from what it finished -- this many times. After that the run ends with a warning that names the step and who must act. Only the steps that collect, correlate and load the web app are started again; never a step that writes to a CMDB, to ServiceNow or to a ticket, and never after the first complete collection. 0 = a failed step is not started again.
settings.purpose: On a new install's first collection, a step that fails or is stopped is started again at once and carries on from what it finished, this many times. After that the run ends with a warning that names the step and who must act.
settings.effect: Higher tries more often before the first collection ends with a warning; 0 means a failed step is not started again. Only the steps that collect, correlate and load the web app are started again -- never a step that writes to a CMDB, to ServiceNow or to a ticket. It has no effect after the first complete collection.
settings.whenToChange: Leave it at 2. Set 0 only when a failed step of the first collection must be looked at before anything is started again.

info.what: On a new install's first collection, a step that fails or is stopped is started again at once and carries on from what it finished, this many times. After that the run ends with a warning that names the step and who must act.
info.whenChanged: Higher tries more often before the first collection ends with a warning; 0 means a failed step is not started again. Only the steps that collect, correlate and load the web app are started again -- never a step that writes to a CMDB, to ServiceNow or to a ticket. It has no effect after the first complete collection.
info.risk: 0: a step that fails on a new install's first collection is not started again, so the first data arrives a run later. Higher: a step that cannot succeed is tried that many times more before the warning. Nothing is written to a CMDB, to ServiceNow or to a ticket by a restart, and nothing is closed. Reversible at once; it applies from the next run and only until the first complete collection.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Leave it at 2. Set 0 only when a failed step of the first collection must be looked at before anything is started again.

settings.name: SI_Pro_Pipeline_GoOnAfterFailedStep
settings.label: Failed step: show what was collected all the same
settings.description: One failed step does not cost the rest of the run: when the correlation or Risk Analysis fails after the collections completed, the data sync and the verification still run on what is stored, so the web app shows what was collected. Nothing is closed, no ticket is changed and no mail is sent from such a run, and it is marked as not complete. $false = every step after a failed one waits for the next good run, as before.
settings.purpose: When the correlation or Risk Analysis fails after the collections completed, the data sync and the verification still run on what is stored, so the web app shows what was collected instead of nothing. The run is marked as not complete and says what is missing.
settings.effect: Off holds every step after a failed one until the next good run, as before: a new install then shows nothing until its first run completes. On or off, nothing is closed, no ticket is changed and no mail is sent from a run that is not complete.
settings.whenToChange: Leave it on. Turn it off only if the web app must never show data of a run in which a step failed.

info.what: When the correlation or Risk Analysis fails after the collections completed, the data sync and the verification still run on what is stored, so the web app shows what was collected instead of nothing. The run is marked as not complete and says what is missing.
info.whenOn: On is the default: it works as described under "What it does".
info.whenOff: Off holds every step after a failed one until the next good run, as before: a new install then shows nothing until its first run completes. On or off, nothing is closed, no ticket is changed and no mail is sent from a run that is not complete.
info.risk: Off: after one failed step the web app gets nothing from that run -- a new install stays empty until its first run completes. On: the web app shows what the completed collections brought, marked as not complete. Either way nothing is closed, no ticket is changed and no mail is sent from a run that is not complete. Reversible at once; it applies from the next run.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Leave it on. Turn it off only if the web app must never show data of a run in which a step failed.

A run in which a report could not be completed and fell back to its last complete result is not shown either, and the pages keep the last complete run. $true = show such a run, marked "a part of this run is from an earlier result".
settings.purpose: Every page shows one run: the last run that completed in full. A run in which a report could not be completed and fell back to its last complete result is not shown by default -- the pages keep the last complete run, so nothing on a page is from two runs.
settings.effect: On: such a run is shown, marked "a part of this run is from an earlier result". Off: the pages keep the last complete run until a run completes in full.
settings.whenToChange: Leave it off. Turn it on only when a report keeps failing and the rest of the newest run must be shown all the same.

info.what: Every page shows one run: the last run that completed in full. A run in which a report could not be completed and fell back to its last complete result is not shown by default -- the pages keep the last complete run, so nothing on a page is from two runs.
info.whenOn: such a run is shown, marked "a part of this run is from an earlier result".
info.whenOff: the pages keep the last complete run until a run completes in full.
info.risk: On: a run in which a report fell back to its last complete result is shown, marked -- a page can then show a part from an earlier run. Reversible at once; it applies from the next run.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Leave it off. Turn it on only when a report keeps failing and the rest of the newest run must be shown all the same.

settings.name: SI_Pro_SourceDropout_AssetDropAction
settings.label: Far fewer assets from a source: what to do
settings.description: A collection that COMPLETES with far fewer assets than the last good one (down by SI_Pro_DataQuality_AssetDropPercent or more): confirm = keep the last good collection and accept the drop by itself when the next complete collection shows the same level (a real clean-up costs one run); accept = take it as it comes, the safety check only reports.
settings.purpose: What happens when a source's collection completes with far fewer assets than its last good collection (down by the data-quality asset drop limit or more). That can be a real clean-up, for example many Azure resources removed, or a source that answered only in part.
settings.effect: confirm: the last good collection is kept (nothing is marked not seen), the run goes on, and the drop is accepted by itself when the next complete collection of that source shows the same level -- a real clean-up takes effect one run later. accept: the collection is taken as it comes and the safety check only reports it.
settings.whenToChange: Set accept when large clean-ups are normal for you and must show at once.

info.what: What happens when a source's collection completes with far fewer assets than its last good collection (down by the data-quality asset drop limit or more). That can be a real clean-up, for example many Azure resources removed, or a source that answered only in part.
info.whenChanged: confirm: the last good collection is kept (nothing is marked not seen), the run goes on, and the drop is accepted by itself when the next complete collection of that source shows the same level -- a real clean-up takes effect one run later. accept: the collection is taken as it comes and the safety check only reports it.
info.risk: Accept: a source that answered only in part is taken as the truth at once -- the assets it no longer lists are marked not seen, and their CIs retire after the usual days. Confirm (the default) costs one run when a clean-up is real. Reversible at once; it applies from the next collection.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Set accept when large clean-ups are normal for you and must show at once.

settings.name: SI_Pro_SourceDropout_HoldDeliveryDays

settings.description: A source whose collection fails does not stop the run: the calculation goes on with that source's last good collection, and every run says how old it is. When a source has had no good collection for this many days or more, delivery waits (no mail, no ticket change) until it collects again; the calculation still goes on. 0 = delivery never waits for a source.
settings.purpose: When the collection of one source (identities, Azure resources, endpoints, the public IP scan) fails, the run goes on with that source's last good collection and says how old it is. When a source has had no good collection for this many days or more, delivery waits: no mail is sent and no ticket is changed until that source collects again.
settings.effect: Lower makes delivery wait sooner; higher lets mails and ticket updates go out longer on older data. 0 means delivery never waits for a source. The calculation always goes on, and nothing is closed or retired because a source is down.
settings.whenToChange: Raise it when a source is known to be down for longer and the mails should keep going out meanwhile.

info.what: When the collection of one source (identities, Azure resources, endpoints, the public IP scan) fails, the run goes on with that source's last good collection and says how old it is. settings.name: SI_RA_PartsInParallel_Max
settings.label: Risk Analysis parts asked at a time (most)
settings.description: The most parts of one Risk Analysis report asked from Defender at a time (the next parts' answers are on their way while a part is processed). Adapts by itself: starts at 2, more while Defender answers quickly, fewer when it asks to slow down. 1 = one part at a time.
settings.purpose: A large Risk Analysis report is asked from Microsoft Defender in parts. While one part is processed (risk scores, the database), the next parts are already asked, so Defender and SecurityInsight work at the same time. This is the most parts asked at a time.
settings.effect: The number adapts by itself: each report starts at 2, asks more while Defender answers quickly, and halves at once when Defender asks to slow down (it then waits as long as Defender says). A higher maximum lets a large report finish sooner when Defender keeps up; 1 asks one part at a time. The parts are processed in their order either way: the stored findings are the same.
settings.whenToChange: Most installs never should. Set 1 only if support asks you to; lower it if other tools in the tenant share Defender's advanced hunting limits.

info.what: A large Risk Analysis report is asked from Microsoft Defender in parts. While one part is processed (risk scores, the database), the next parts are already asked, so Defender and SecurityInsight work at the same time. This is the most parts asked at a time.
info.whenChanged: The number adapts by itself: each report starts at 2, asks more while Defender answers quickly, and halves at once when Defender asks to slow down (it then waits as long as Defender says). A higher maximum lets a large report finish sooner when Defender keeps up; 1 asks one part at a time. The parts are processed in their order either way: the stored findings are the same.
info.risk: Only changes how many parts of a report are asked from Defender at a time, so how long Risk Analysis takes: 1 makes a large report take much longer; a higher number can make Defender ask SecurityInsight to slow down more often (it then does). The findings are the same either way. Reversible at once.
info.recommended: Keep 6 (the default).

settings.name: SI_Shodan_ForceFreshScan
settings.label: Shodan fresh scans
settings.defaultText: Off: cached and existing Shodan data only, no scan credits spent.
settings.description: Set ForceFreshScan = $true and schedule the launcher to run at 02:00 + 03:00 (and optionally 04:00). First run submits + waits up to 5 min, persisting scan_id to data/shodan-pending-scans.json if it can't sync-complete. Later runs check pending state + a skip-if-recent guard (data/shodan-last-fresh-scan.json) so credits don't burn on duplicate submits. Defaults are OFF -- cache-only mode -- so passive enrichment doesn't burn scan credits. Turn ON in LauncherConfig.custom.ps1 when you want fresh data.

settings.defaultText: Taken from SpnClientId or the platform; if none, managed identity
settings.description: Service principal instead: set SI_AuthMethod = 'Certificate' (recommended) or 'Secret', then fill in the app below.
settings.purpose: Application (client) id of the service principal the engines sign in as when not using managed identity.
settings.effect: Decides which app registration reads data and ingests results; that app needs the required Graph, Azure and Log Analytics permissions. Without it, no service principal sign-in happens.

info.risk: Affects how the jobs sign in or which Azure resources they use. A wrong value stops the affected jobs at their next run (nothing is changed or deleted); a broader identity or right gives the jobs more access than they need. Reversible: correct it and run again.
info.default: Looked up from the app id at run start
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Only when the automatic lookup fails because the signing-in identity cannot read service principals.

settings.name: SI_SPN_Secret
settings.label: Service principal client secret

These four are REQUIRED. Bootstrap-Auth.ps1 pulls them from KV when blank.
settings.purpose: The Entra tenant the service principal signs in to, for data reads and Log Analytics ingestion.

info.default: Taken from SpnTenantId, the platform, or the managed identity's sign-in
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Set during setup when you use a service principal.

settings.name: SI_SqlPacing_Enabled
settings.label: Slow down large writes when the database is busy
settings.description: DATABASE WRITE PACE: the large writers (Risk Analysis storing its findings, the data sync preparing the views, the removal of old collections) read how busy the database is before each batch. Above the high mark (the highest of log write, data reads and CPU, in percent of the tier) they pause and write smaller batches; below the low mark they go back to full pace. Nothing is left out -- only slower while the database is saturated. On by default; $false switches it off.
settings.purpose: Whether the large database writers (Risk Analysis storing its findings, the data sync preparing the views, the removal of old collections) look at how busy the database is before each batch.
settings.effect: On: while the database is at its limit (log write, data reads or CPU above the high mark), each writer pauses before its next batch and writes smaller batches, so the web app and the other jobs keep a share; below the low mark it writes at full pace again. Nothing is left out -- the same rows are written, only slower while the database is saturated. Off: the writers always write at full pace.
settings.whenToChange: Leave it on. Switch it off only if support asks you to.

info.what: Whether the large database writers (Risk Analysis storing its findings, the data sync preparing the views, the removal of old collections) look at how busy the database is before each batch.
info.whenOn: while the database is at its limit (log write, data reads or CPU above the high mark), each writer pauses before its next batch and writes smaller batches, so the web app and the other jobs keep a share; below the low mark it writes at full pace again. Nothing is left out -- the same rows are written, only slower while the database is saturated.
info.whenOff: the writers always write at full pace.
info.risk: Off: on a busy database the large writers keep it at its limit for as long as the daily run writes, and the web app is slow meanwhile. No data is changed either way. Reversible at once.
info.recommended: On (the default).

settings.name: SI_SqlPacing_HighPercent
settings.label: Database busy above (percent)
settings.description: The database load (percent) above which the writers slow down. Default 85.
settings.purpose: The database load (the highest of log write, data reads and CPU, in percent of what its tier allows) above which the large writers slow down.
settings.effect: Lower: the writers make room for the web app sooner, and a full run takes longer on a busy database. Higher: the writers keep their pace until the database is closer to its limit. A value that is not a number from 1 to 100 uses 85.
settings.whenToChange: Lower it if the web app is slow during the daily run; raise it if the run must finish sooner and nobody uses the web app then.

info.what: The database load (the highest of log write, data reads and CPU, in percent of what its tier allows) above which the large writers slow down.
info.whenChanged: Lower: the writers make room for the web app sooner, and a full run takes longer on a busy database. Higher: the writers keep their pace until the database is closer to its limit. A value that is not a number from 1 to 100 uses 85.
info.risk: Only changes how soon the large writers slow down: a lower value gives the web app more room and makes a full run take longer on a busy database. No data is changed. Reversible at once.
info.requires: Works only while "Slow down large writes when the database is busy" is on.
info.recommended: Keep 85.

settings.name: SI_SqlPacing_LowPercent
settings.label: Database calm again below (percent)
settings.description: The database load (percent) below which they go back to full pace. Default 70; must be below the high mark.
settings.purpose: The database load below which the large writers go back to their full pace after they slowed down.
settings.effect: Between this and the busy mark a writer keeps the pause it has. Must be below the busy mark; a value at or above it uses the busy mark minus 15.
settings.whenToChange: Rarely. Lower it if the writers speed up and slow down again and again.

info.what: The database load below which the large writers go back to their full pace after they slowed down.
info.whenChanged: Between this and the busy mark a writer keeps the pause it has. Must be below the busy mark; a value at or above it uses the busy mark minus 15.
info.risk: Only changes when the large writers go back to full pace. No data is changed. Reversible at once.
info.requires: Works only while "Slow down large writes when the database is busy" is on.
info.recommended: Keep 70.

settings.purpose: The storage account the collection engines use for staging data, caches, the shared catalog and the identity ledger.

info.default: Same resource group as the workspace (or the data collection rules)
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Only when your storage account lives in a different resource group from the workspace; setup normally writes it.

settings.name: SI_SystemPrompt_azure

settings.name: SI_TableNamePattern

settings.description: v2.2 LA table + DCR naming patterns. {0} placeholder is filled with engine name. Defaults: 'SI_{0}_Profile' + 'dcr-si-{0}-profile'. Override only if you maintain a parallel naming scheme.

settings.name: SI_Telemetry_Enabled
settings.label: Status reports to Invardia
settings.description: One status report a day and one short report per engine run (which engine, ok / warning / failed, how long, the stage and the kind of error). Community: anonymous -- a random install id, no tenant, no host name, no error text, counts only as ranges. Pro: identified by the install key, with the error text shortened and secrets removed. On by default; $false sends nothing at all.
settings.purpose: Whether the install sends Invardia one status report a day and one short report per engine run: which engine ran, whether it ended ok, with warnings or failed, how long it took, the stage and the kind of error. Community reports are anonymous (a random install id; no tenant, host name or error text; counts only as ranges). Pro reports are identified by the install key and carry the error text with secrets removed.
settings.effect: Off sends nothing at all: no report is built, no file is written and Invardia is never contacted for this. For Pro, Invardia then cannot see failed or silent runs and warn you about them.
settings.whenToChange: Turn it off if your organisation does not allow status reports to leave the environment.

info.what: Whether the install sends Invardia one status report a day and one short report per engine run: which engine ran, whether it ended ok, with warnings or failed, how long it took, the stage and the kind of error. Community reports are anonymous (a random install id; no tenant, host name or error text; counts only as ranges). Pro reports are identified by the install key and carry the error text with secrets removed.
info.whenOn: On is the default: it works as described under "What it does".
info.whenOff: Off sends nothing at all: no report is built, no file is written and Invardia is never contacted for this. For Pro, Invardia then cannot see failed or silent runs and warn you about them.
info.risk: Changes how long data is kept or how quickly assets are treated as gone. Shortening a retention DELETES older data at the next clean-up and that cannot be undone; shortening a grace period retires assets (and closes their findings) sooner. Lengthening is safe but uses more storage.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Turn it off if your organisation does not allow status reports to leave the environment.

settings.name: SI_Telemetry_Endpoint
settings.label: Status report address
