settings.purpose: The https address the status reports are sent to.
settings.effect: Reports go to this address instead. Only https addresses are used; anything else sends nothing.
settings.whenToChange: Practically never; only if Invardia tells you to use another address.

info.what: The https address the status reports are sent to.
info.whenChanged: Reports go to this address instead. Only https addresses are used; anything else sends nothing.
info.risk: A tuning or diagnostic setting: it mostly changes run time, cost or log detail. Leave it at the default unless support asks. Reversible at once.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Practically never; only if Invardia tells you to use another address.

settings.name: SI_Telemetry_SendEndpoints
settings.label: Send this install's links to Invardia
settings.defaultText: On -- switch it off to send no links
settings.description: Whether the daily status report (Pro, with an install key) carries this install's own links -- the web app's and the MCP server's addresses -- so Invardia's mails about this environment can open it. On by default; switch it off to send no links.
settings.purpose: Pro installs with an install key can send Invardia this install's own links -- the web app's and the MCP server's addresses -- with the daily status report, so every mail Invardia sends about this environment carries an Open SecurityInsight button. Only the addresses are sent: no names, no secrets.
settings.effect: On: the daily status report carries the web app's and the MCP server's addresses (read from the install's own hosting). Off: it carries no links. A failed run's report links to the run health page either way.
settings.whenToChange: Switch it off only if Invardia should not see this install's web app and MCP addresses.

info.what: Pro installs with an install key can send Invardia this install's own links -- the web app's and the MCP server's addresses -- with the daily status report, so every mail Invardia sends about this environment carries an Open SecurityInsight button. Only the addresses are sent: no names, no secrets.
info.whenOn: the daily status report carries the web app's and the MCP server's addresses (read from the install's own hosting).
info.whenOff: it carries no links. A failed run's report links to the run health page either way.
info.risk: Changes only what Invardia sees: the web app's and the MCP server's addresses; nothing in your tenant changes. Reversible at once.
info.default: On -- switch it off to send no links
info.recommended: Keep the default (on).

settings.name: SI_Telemetry_SendHealth
settings.label: Send the data health result to Invardia
settings.defaultText: On -- switch it off to send nothing about data health
settings.description: Send the daily data health result (counts only) to Invardia. On by default; switched off, nothing about data health is sent.
settings.purpose: Pro installs with an install key send Invardia the daily data health result -- the state and, per source and report, how many records were checked, found, missing and different. Counts only: no names, ids or values.
settings.effect: On: every daily check, and at once when the state changes, the counts go to Invardia, which uses them to hold an update ring from moving on. Off: nothing about data health is sent.
settings.whenToChange: Keep it on. Switch it off only if your organisation does not allow the data health counts to leave the environment.

info.what: Pro installs with an install key send Invardia the daily data health result -- the state and, per source and report, how many records were checked, found, missing and different. Counts only: no names, ids or values.
info.whenOn: every daily check, and at once when the state changes, the counts go to Invardia, which uses them to hold an update ring from moving on.
info.whenOff: nothing about data health is sent.
info.risk: On: the daily data health counts go to Invardia (no names or ids); an Unhealthy install then holds the update ring from moving on. Off: Invardia does not know the data health of this install. Reversible at once.
info.default: On -- switch it off to send nothing about data health
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Keep it on. Switch it off only if your organisation does not allow the data health counts to leave the environment.

settings.name: SI_Telemetry_SetupControls
settings.label: Setup report to Invardia
settings.defaultText: all: every control, SecurityInsight's own too (sent again with only the minimum list when Invardia does not take it)
settings.description: Which controls the daily setup report to Invardia carries (Pro, with an install key): 'all' (default) = the framework's minimum control list and SecurityInsight's own controls (when Invardia does not take that report, it goes again once with only the minimum list); 'minimum' = only the framework's minimum list; 'off' = no setup report.
settings.purpose: Pro installs with an install key send Invardia one setup report a day: a list of critical settings (updater, update ring, install key, licence, mail, permissions, last run, backup) with ok / missing / wrong / unknown, so Invardia can see what is not set up and help you. No secrets, no names of people and no error text are sent.
settings.effect: 'all' (the default) sends the minimum list every product shares and SecurityInsight's own controls (SQL database reachable, job layout, run limits, last daily run, data sources, last CI build, Log Analytics ingestion, licence edition); when Invardia does not take that report, it is sent again once with only the minimum list, and the run log says so. 'minimum' sends only the minimum list. 'off' sends no setup report; the daily status report and the run reports are not affected. Status reports to Invardia off (SI_Telemetry_Enabled) turns this off too.
settings.whenToChange: Keep 'all'. Choose 'minimum' to send only the shared list, or 'off' if your organisation does not allow the setup state to leave the environment.
settings.hint: all = also SecurityInsight's own controls (default). minimum = the shared control list only. off = no setup report.

info.what: Pro installs with an install key send Invardia one setup report a day: a list of critical settings (updater, update ring, install key, licence, mail, permissions, last run, backup) with ok / missing / wrong / unknown, so Invardia can see what is not set up and help you. No secrets, no names of people and no error text are sent.
info.whenChanged: 'all' (the default) sends the minimum list every product shares and SecurityInsight's own controls (SQL database reachable, job layout, run limits, last daily run, data sources, last CI build, Log Analytics ingestion, licence edition); when Invardia does not take that report, it is sent again once with only the minimum list, and the run log says so. 'minimum' sends only the minimum list. 'off' sends no setup report; the daily status report and the run reports are not affected. Status reports to Invardia off (SI_Telemetry_Enabled) turns this off too.
info.risk: Changes only what Invardia sees about this install's setup; nothing in your tenant changes. When Invardia does not take the full list ('all'), the report goes again once with the minimum list; the daily status report and the run reports are not affected. 'off' means Invardia cannot see a missing setting and offer help.
info.default: all: every control, SecurityInsight's own too (sent again with only the minimum list when Invardia does not take it)
info.recommended: Keep the default (all).

settings.name: SI_TenantDomain

settings.purpose: Tenant domain shown in report mail subjects and used in the Azure portal links Risk Analysis adds to findings on Azure resources.

settings.name: SI_Throttle_StuckHours
settings.label: Stuck on throttling after (hours)
settings.description: THROTTLE-IS-NORMAL: a run Microsoft only throttled is shown as throttled, is never mailed and runs again at its next scheduled time. The ONE alert ("stuck") goes out when a job has been throttled on every run for this many hours, or this many runs in a row -- whichever comes first, never on one run alone. The next run that completes clears it.
settings.purpose: How long a job may keep being throttled by Microsoft, without completing, before the one "stuck" alert is sent.
settings.effect: A throttled run is normal: it is shown as throttled, it is not mailed, and the job runs again at its next scheduled time. When a job has been throttled on every run for this many hours (and at least two runs), one alert says it is stuck. Whichever comes first of this and the number of runs below. The next run that completes clears it.
settings.whenToChange: Raise it if you get the alert for jobs that catch up by themselves; lower it if you need to know sooner.

info.what: How long a job may keep being throttled by Microsoft, without completing, before the one "stuck" alert is sent.
info.whenChanged: A throttled run is normal: it is shown as throttled, it is not mailed, and the job runs again at its next scheduled time. When a job has been throttled on every run for this many hours (and at least two runs), one alert says it is stuck. Whichever comes first of this and the number of runs below. The next run that completes clears it.
info.risk: A safety check protects your data from a broken run; changing it changes when a step is held or stopped. Reversible at once.
info.requires: Works only while "Job stuck on throttling" is on.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Raise it if you get the alert for jobs that catch up by themselves; lower it if you need to know sooner.

settings.name: SI_Throttle_StuckRuns
settings.label: Stuck on throttling after (runs)
settings.description: How many throttled runs in a row, without one that completes, send the one "stuck" alert (whichever comes first).
settings.purpose: How many throttled runs in a row, without one that completes, send the one "stuck" alert.
settings.effect: When a job has been throttled this many runs in a row, one alert says it is stuck -- whichever comes first of this and the number of hours above. The next run that completes clears it.
settings.whenToChange: Raise it for jobs that run very often; lower it if you need to know sooner.

info.what: How many throttled runs in a row, without one that completes, send the one "stuck" alert.
info.whenChanged: When a job has been throttled this many runs in a row, one alert says it is stuck -- whichever comes first of this and the number of hours above. The next run that completes clears it.
info.risk: A safety check protects your data from a broken run; changing it changes when a step is held or stopped. Reversible at once.
info.requires: Works only while "Job stuck on throttling" is on.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Raise it for jobs that run very often; lower it if you need to know sooner.

settings.name: SI_TierCadence_Default
settings.label: Re-check interval, unknown tier
settings.description: used when cached tier is null/unknown
settings.purpose: How often an asset whose privilege tier is not yet known is re-processed when the per-asset skip schedule is in use.

settings.name: SI_Trend_AtEndOfRiskAnalysis
settings.label: Write the risk trend at the end of Risk Analysis
settings.description: Risk Analysis writes the day's risk trend row itself at the end of a summary run (the trend job is then not needed).
settings.purpose: Whether a Risk Analysis summary run writes the day's risk trend row itself, from the rows it has just published.
settings.effect: On: one trend row per day, written by Risk Analysis -- the separate risk trend job is not needed and waits for a run by hand. Off: no trend row unless the risk trend job runs. A run that was partial writes no row (a gap, not a drop).

info.what: Whether a Risk Analysis summary run writes the day's risk trend row itself, from the rows it has just published.

info.risk: Changes when or whether jobs run: a job that does not run leaves its data older until it runs again. Reversible at once; nothing already collected is changed.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Only when you run the risk trend job on its own schedule instead.

info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Only when the default rule name clashes with an existing one in your workspace.

info.whenOn: Run logs become much longer and more detailed, which helps support find problems. Collected data and reports are unchanged.
info.whenOff: normal log detail.

settings.name: SI_VulnSync_CloseAfterRuns
settings.label: Runs before a vulnerability closes
settings.description: How many complete runs in a row a vulnerability must be missing from an asset before the close-loop closes it as fixed. Each run only counts when the asset itself was seen in that run with its vulnerability data; a run in which the asset was not seen counts for nothing and keeps the vulnerability open. Default 2, at least 1. Raise it if devices report a vulnerability on and off.
settings.purpose: How many complete runs in a row a vulnerability must be missing from an asset that was seen before the close-loop marks it fixed.
settings.effect: Higher avoids closing and reopening vulnerabilities that devices report on and off, but confirms real fixes later. Runs where the asset was not seen do not count. Below 1 is raised to 1; non-numbers use 2.
settings.whenToChange: Raise it if vulnerabilities keep closing and reopening on the same devices.

info.what: How many complete runs in a row a vulnerability must be missing from an asset that was seen before the close-loop marks it fixed.
info.whenChanged: Higher avoids closing and reopening vulnerabilities that devices report on and off, but confirms real fixes later. Runs where the asset was not seen do not count. Below 1 is raised to 1; non-numbers use 2.
info.risk: Changes how long data is kept or how quickly assets are treated as gone. Shortening a retention DELETES older data at the next clean-up and that cannot be undone; shortening a grace period retires assets (and closes their findings) sooner. Lengthening is safe but uses more storage.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Raise it if vulnerabilities keep closing and reopening on the same devices.

settings.name: SI_VulnSync_CollapseFloor
settings.label: Vulnerabilities: share that must still be reported
settings.description: The share of the open records that must still be reported (0 to 1).
settings.purpose: The share (0 to 1) of the open vulnerability records the newest results must still report before anything may close.
settings.effect: When fewer of the open records are still reported, the run looks like a partial collection and closes nothing. 0 switches this check off; 1 forbids every close.
settings.whenToChange: Lower it if your estate legitimately shrinks a lot between runs.

info.what: The share (0 to 1) of the open vulnerability records the newest results must still report before anything may close.
info.whenChanged: When fewer of the open records are still reported, the run looks like a partial collection and closes nothing. 0 switches this check off; 1 forbids every close.
info.risk: A safety check protects your data from a broken run; changing it changes when a step is held or stopped. Reversible at once.
info.requires: Works only while "Vulnerabilities: result far smaller than usual" is on. A SecurityInsight Pro licence.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Lower it if your estate legitimately shrinks a lot between runs.

settings.name: SI_VulnSync_MaxCloseAbsolute
settings.label: Vulnerability close limit (number of records)
settings.defaultText: 0 = no limit on the number (only the share counts)
settings.description: The number limit: 0 = none (the default for vulnerabilities).
settings.purpose: An optional limit on HOW MANY vulnerability records the connector may close in one run, on top of the share above.
settings.effect: 0: only the share of the open records decides -- a patch round that closes hundreds of records out of thousands goes through. Above 0: a run that would close more records than this is held as well.
settings.whenToChange: Leave it at 0 for vulnerabilities. Set a number only if you want a hard cap regardless of the size of your estate.

info.what: An optional limit on HOW MANY vulnerability records the connector may close in one run, on top of the share above.
info.whenChanged: 0: only the share of the open records decides -- a patch round that closes hundreds of records out of thousands goes through. Above 0: a run that would close more records than this is held as well.
info.risk: A safety check protects your data from a broken run; changing it changes when a step is held or stopped. Reversible at once.
info.requires: Works only while "Vulnerability close limit" is on. A SecurityInsight Pro licence.
info.default: 0 = no limit on the number (only the share counts)
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Leave it at 0 for vulnerabilities. Set a number only if you want a hard cap regardless of the size of your estate.

settings.name: SI_VulnSync_MaxClosePercent
settings.label: Vulnerability close limit (% of open records)
settings.description: The vulnerability close limit: the share of the open records (default 10), an optional number (default 0 = no number limit -- a patch round closes hundreds), and the share that must still be reported (0 to 1, default 0.5).
settings.purpose: The largest share of the open vulnerability records the connector may close in one run before it holds the closes for an Admin to release.
settings.effect: A run that would close more than this share of the open records closes none of them and holds them (Guards page: release once). Only the records that really close count -- not first absences, held or out-of-scope records, and not closes a fresh Defender assessment confirms.
settings.whenToChange: Raise it if your patch rounds regularly fix more than this share at once.

info.what: The largest share of the open vulnerability records the connector may close in one run before it holds the closes for an Admin to release.
info.whenChanged: A run that would close more than this share of the open records closes none of them and holds them (Guards page: release once). Only the records that really close count -- not first absences, held or out-of-scope records, and not closes a fresh Defender assessment confirms.
info.risk: A safety check protects your data from a broken run; changing it changes when a step is held or stopped. Reversible at once.
info.requires: Works only while "Vulnerability close limit" is on. A SecurityInsight Pro licence.
info.recommended: Keep the default. Change it when: Raise it if your patch rounds regularly fix more than this share at once.

settings.name: WhatIfMode
settings.label: Dry run
settings.description: Dry run. Here, in the configuration, only asset tagging reads it (report only, no tag changed). Every other engine ignores it here and publishes as normal; start that one run with -WhatIfMode for a dry run instead.
settings.purpose: Requests a run that shows what would change without changing anything.
settings.effect: In the configuration it is read only by asset tagging, which then only reports the tags it would apply or remove. Every other engine ignores it in the configuration (scheduled runs always publish, and each run says the value was ignored): a dry run of profiling, Risk Analysis or the tier classifier is asked for per run -- start the launcher with -WhatIfMode, or set SI_WHATIF=1 on one container job execution. Such a run says so at its start and its end. Profiling and Risk Analysis then write their results to local files only -- nothing goes to Log Analytics, the mail, the export location or the caches; the run-health record says dry run. The tier classifier writes its result beside the catalog, never over it.
settings.whenToChange: In the configuration: only before the first real asset-tagging run. To preview any other engine, use -WhatIfMode on that one run.

info.what: Requests a run that shows what would change without changing anything.
info.whenOn: In the configuration it is read only by asset tagging, which then only reports the tags it would apply or remove. Such a run says so at its start and its end. Profiling and Risk Analysis then write their results to local files only -- nothing goes to Log Analytics, the mail, the export location or the caches; the run-health record says dry run. The tier classifier writes its result beside the catalog, never over it.
info.whenOff: a normal run.
